title: 《高等微積分》第 1 集｜邏輯、量詞與連接詞｜Loomis & Sternberg 第 0 章 §1-3
description:
本集對應 Loomis 與 Sternberg《Advanced Calculus》第 0 章第 1 到 3 節（書頁 1 到 6）。

作者說第 0 章主要是給人回頭查閱用的，但其中有一件事非讀不可：量詞的順序。

先分清楚兩個東西。一個句子如果當下就能判斷真假，叫做敘述；含有變數、要給了值才能判斷的，叫做敘述框架。從框架變出敘述有兩條路：給變數一個值，或是加上量詞。宣告它永遠為真，就是全稱量詞；宣告它有時為真，就是存在量詞。被量詞綁住的變數叫束縛變數，沒被綁住的叫自由變數。

本集的重點在中段。當兩種量詞混用時，寫的順序會改變整句話的意思。書上的例子是：「對每一個 x 都存在一個 y 使得 x 小於 y」是真的，y 取 x 加一就行；但「存在一個 y 使得對每一個 x 都有 x 小於 y」是假的，因為那個 y 加一就不小於它自己。差別在於第一句的 y 可以跟著 x 改變，第二句卻要求同一個 y 對所有 x 都成立，所以第二句強得多。作者在這裡寫了一句很重的話：讀者必須把這一點弄得絕對清楚，他往後的整個數學生涯都繫於此。

反過來，同一種量詞連在一起時順序不影響意思。收斂與連續的定義都用到三個量詞，形式完全一樣。

後半是連接詞。「而且」只有兩邊都真才真；「或」在數學裡永遠是相容的，至少一個真、兩個都真也算。最麻煩的是「如果就」：因為「若 x 小於三則 x 小於五」對每一個 x 都成立，我們被迫承認前提為假時整句話仍然是真的，所以只有真推出假才是假的。真值表永遠為真的形式叫恆真式。

最後是量詞的否定：取否定時把每個量詞換成相反的那一種，再把否定號移到整串的最後面。

本影片為雙語教學動畫系列（繁體中文版）。

title: Advanced Calculus, Episode 1 | Logic, Quantifiers and the Connectives | Ch. 0, §1-3
description:
This episode covers chapter 0, sections 1 to 3 (pages 1 to 6) of Loomis and Sternberg's Advanced Calculus.

The authors say chapter 0 is mainly there to be referred back to, but one thing in it must be read: the order of quantifiers.

First the distinction. A sentence that is true or false as it stands is a statement; one containing a variable is a statement frame. There are two ways to turn a frame into a statement: give the variable a value, or quantify it. Asserting that it is always true gives the universal quantifier; asserting that it is sometimes true gives the existential quantifier. A quantified variable is called bound, an unquantified one free.

The heart of the episode is in the middle. When quantifiers of both kinds are used, the order in which they are written changes what the sentence says. The book's example: for every x there exists a y with x less than y is true, taking y to be x plus one; but there exists a y such that for every x, x is less than y is false, because that y plus one is not less than itself. In the first the y may change with x; the second demands a single y that works for every x, which is far stronger. The authors put it bluntly: the reader must be absolutely clear on this point, his whole mathematical future is at stake.

Among quantifiers of the same kind, order does not matter. Convergence and continuity both need three quantifiers and have exactly the same shape.

The second half is the connectives. And is true only when both sides are; or in mathematics is always inclusive. The troublesome one is if-then: since if x is less than three then x is less than five holds for every x, we must accept that the sentence is true whenever the premise is false, so it is false only when true implies false. A form whose truth table is always true is a tautology.

Finally, negating a string of quantifiers: change each quantifier to the opposite kind and move the negation sign to the end of the string.

Part of a bilingual animated teaching series (English edition).
